decisions.reason: F2 incorrectly identifies every algebra generated by the empty list with its base ring: Z/2 over Z is a counterexample. The only empty-list use in step 2.1 is the identity A→A, which is valid; the finite polynomial-chart cover proves the unchanged statement.

F11 falsely presents the function-field supplier as proving existence of a generic point. The Statement and Given already supply η_X, so step 2.1 obtains uniqueness from the proved T0 property without that appeal. Corrected F11 and the attribution; no mathematical conclusion is lost. The unused F11 fact and dependency were then removed entirely.

The title suggests an isomorphism on the full inverse image, whereas the exact Statement already asserts only f^{-1}(V_0)∩U→V_0. For the doubled-origin line, either affine chart maps identically to A1 and gives σ=1, but the whole map has two origins. Retitled to match the existing valid chart conclusion, without weakening or changing the Statement.

The displayed 1⊗b_i is ill-typed in B⊗_A A′; b_i belongs in the first tensor factor. Replaced it by b_i⊗1 and wrote the balancing identity b⊗a′=Σ(b_i⊗1)(1⊗ρ(a_i)a′). This local correction proves the intended finite generation with no change in hypotheses or proof route.

Step 2.2 treats ideal generators as algebra generators without supplying their arbitrary coefficients. In A=k[x,x^{-1}], B=C=k and x↦1, the fiber product identifies with A; the proposed generator (x−1,0) generates only k[x−1], which excludes (x^{-1},1). This is a genuine finite-type proof gap, not a citation defect. Added compatible lifts of algebra generators of A and B so both projections of the generated subalgebra are surjective; these supply coefficients for the kernel ideal generators and prove it is the entire fiber product.

reviews.reason: Corrected F2 to use the image of the structure map. Checked all eight direct dependency interfaces, the owning contract and page: n+1 polynomial charts give local finite type and quasi-compactness over each affine base, including n=0 and empty base. Only finite selections occur, so no AC is introduced. This is an author repair review, not independent review of the new text.

Checked direct supplier statements, contract and common home page. Finite affine Noetherian cover proves Noetherianness; prime-inclusion specialization proves T0. Under AC minimal bad closed subsets yield finite irreducible decomposition. A proper positive-dimensional component would extend to a length-two chain in X; zero-dimensional T0 irreducible components are single closed points. Generic uniqueness uses the given η_X. Contract summaries now retain T0. This reviews my repair, not an independent rejudgment. Re-examined the proof after deleting unused F11 and its function-field dependency: no remaining step uses function fields; all statements and AC premises remain unchanged. Final rereview reconciled step 7.1 with step 5.1: the empty closed set is included, while dimensions other than one are excluded.

Reviewed all dependency interfaces and the contract/page. The generic stalk isomorphism injects B into A inside the common fraction field; the finite product of nonzero denominators makes B_σ→A_σ both surjective and injective, including the empty generator list. Replaced F9 and its dependency with the published scheme-level localization open-immersion lemma, since a topological homeomorphism alone does not justify step 5.1 as a scheme isomorphism. Statement unchanged; this is my repair review, not independent review.

Checked direct dependencies, contract and page: affine base-change charts are Spec(B⊗_A A′), generated over A′ by b_i⊗1; the stated AC-dependent target-local criterion makes the map finite. For composition, products of two finite module generating lists generate over the final base, without AC. Empty and zero-ring charts are included. The corrected tensor identity is an author repair, not an independent rejudgment.

Checked the full argument, all direct supplier interfaces, contract and home page. Corrected chart generators give finite type; the two proper closed components give quasi-compactness, and their affine intersections give quasi-separatedness. A valuation-ring map whose generic point lies in a closed component kills its defining ideal because the target ring is a domain, so every lift factors through that component. Its properness supplies existence and uniqueness. Made component quasi-separatedness explicit, limited the localization assertion to principal localization, and included F3 in the existing AC accounting. Statement unchanged. This is my repair review, not independent review of the new proof.
